title: Where to drink in Akihabara
desc: Twelve real bars in and around Akihabara: craft beer, standing bars and sake, with hours, how to pay, a sketch map, and the Japanese name to show at the door.
lead: Twelve real places near Akihabara and Kanda. Hours are shown for today in Tokyo. Show the Japanese name at the door if you need to.
foot: Hours, closed days and payment come from Tabelog, checked on 9 Nov 2026. Shops change them without notice, and public holidays can differ, so check the listing on the map before you go.
The legal drinking age in Japan is 20. Some places may ask for ID. Several bars here take cash only, so carry some yen.
Walking times are from the nearest station and are approximate.

g1.name: Akihabara
g1.note: Seven places within about 8 minutes on foot of Akihabara Station, or less.

g2.name: Kanda side
g2.note: Kanda is one stop from Akihabara on the JR line. The first two are on the way, about 5 min on foot from Akihabara.

know: Hours and days off can change. Check the listing on the map before you go.
The legal drinking age in Japan is 20. Some places may ask for ID.
Several bars here take cash only: iBrew, Craft Beer Scissors and Beer Otaku Spice (PayPay is the only cashless option there). Carry some yen.
Izakaya often add a small seating charge. Beer Otaku Spice does in the evening. Fujita Saketen has none.
Bar Malt Road is closed on Sundays, public holidays and the third Monday. Fujita Saketen is open on weekdays only, from 17:00 to 21:00.
